content_preview.title: FDA Advisory Committee Backs Replimune's RP1 Melanoma Therapy in 10-3 Vote After Two Prior Rejections
content_preview.summary: An FDA panel voted 10-3 that IGNYTE trial results for RP1 plus nivolumab are clinically meaningful, days ahead of an August 2 decision.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

An FDA advisory committee voted 10 to 3 on July 30 that efficacy results from Replimune's IGNYTE trial are "evaluable and clinically meaningful," backing the company's oncolytic virus therapy RP1 for advanced melanoma after two prior rejections of the same application, according to [Replimune](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/30/3336537/0/en/replimune-announces-favorable-outcome-of-fda-s-cellular-tissue-and-gene-therapies-advisory-committee-meeting-for-rp1-in-advan...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (777 words, within the 400-1200 range) covering an FDA advisory committee vote on Replimune's RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) plus nivolumab for advanced melanoma. Clear sectioning (Overview, What the Committee Voted On, A Third Attempt After Two Rejections, Company Response, What We Don't Know) with balanced attribution of both supportive and dissenting committee views.

The two articles share some background statistics (e.g., the OS/ORR figures) by necessity since both describe the same underlying IGNYTE dataset, but the June article's lead and thesis is the survival data/resubmission announcement while this article's lead and thesis is the vote itself.

No sensationalism or promotional language despite two press-release-adjacent sources (GlobeNewswire, StockTitan) being among the citations.
